cards.bank: Caixa Geral de Depósitos Cabo Verde
Caixa Geral de Depósitos Cabo Verde

note: Cabo Verde's largest bank, the Banco Comercial do Atlântico, was read; the Caixa Económica's and Banco Interatlântico's price lists weren't reached. The BCA's price list (in force from 30 July 2026), read in full for its credit cards: the BCA Visa Classic and Gold cost 4,000 and 7,000 escudos a year for the main card, charge a nominal 18.250% a year (22.345% effective), 221 escudos plus 1% for a cash advance in Cabo Verde (331 plus 1% abroad; the domestic one is written), 1.7% on purchases outside Cabo Verde and 1% of the amount over the limit. Stamp duty of 3.5% is added to every fee and to the interest, written as tax (this file wrote the Classic's fee with its stamp duty, 4,140, before the form had a tax term); the further 0.05% stamp duty on the month's average balance has no form in the game and isn't written. The late payment charge (331 escudos plus 2%) doesn't say 2% of what, so it isn't written; nor is the 1% charged on a change of limit, whose base isn't stated. The corporate card isn't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: Caixa Geral de Depósitos Cabo Verde (the bank at bi.cv, which the earlier note called Banco Interatlântico) was added, the next large bank whose price list is on its site: its commissions and interest rate leaflets (each in force from 11 October 2026), read for its personal credit cards: the Visa Gold and Visa Classic cost 8,500 and 4,000 escudos a year for the main card, issue free, charge at most 18% and 19% a year (TAN, the leaflet's maximum, written at it), 1% plus 250 escudos for a cash advance at an ATM in Cabo Verde (350 at a counter; the ATM one is written), 1,000 escudos for a missed payment and 1% of the amount over the limit, at most 3,000. Stamp duty of 3.5% on fees and interest is written as tax; the further 0.050% on the month's average balance isn't written, as for the BCA. The 1.5% and 2% charged on 'pagamento de serviços' at home and abroad aren't written, the leaflet not saying they fall on every purchase; the late interest surcharge of at most 2% a year applies only to capital overdue and isn't written as a penalty rate. The Caixa Económica de Cabo Verde's site links no price list that could be found (its /precario page answered 404) and the Banco Cabo-Verdiano de Negócios' site answered a captcha. So Cabo Verde has two banks' cards. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: the BCA's adhesion form for its Visa credit cards (Classic and Gold) offers automatic payment of 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or 100%, written as 10%, the least. Banco Interatlântico's adhesion proposal for its Visa credit cards (the Caixa Geral de Depósitos group's bank, whose price lists are already cited) offers 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of the balance owed, at least 7,000 escudos on the Classic and 10,000 on the Gold, written as 10% with those floors.
